[A10] Observed during manager cancellation of an obsolete source-validation run for #517. This is an existing gPTP plane verification-driver issue, outside that issue's ordinary milan_dp pooling change.

## Objective and evidence

A stopped full-sweep validation clone must not retain a deliberately broken tracked RTL file, and graceful cancellation must not launch later suites while shutdown is in progress.

At source `7ab1c8d0ad073fbc1977c455dea89b7b318d4e52`, stopping the manager-owned native unit left exactly the `age_never_expires` mutation from `tb/verilator/gptp_shadow/mutants.py` in `hdl/ieee8021as/gptp_plane/KL_gptp_txret.sv`: `age_hit_w` was prefixed with `1'b0 &&`. The subsequent preparation's dirty-tree guard correctly refused that clone. The source branch and user checkout were clean. The original native run remains partial, not PASS.

[Exact residue, original/pristine file hashes and bounded recovery](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/491c5992161cf3dbb5a52ad2d8f9862553b591d1/review-evidence/517-r1/stopped-native-residue). [Stopped sweep output](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/630e01f206e802dc5c4a6f58eb3a536e1684b05b/review-evidence/517-r1/first-source-incomplete).

The current mutation driver modifies the tracked source, waits for make, and restores only afterward, without a signal cleanup boundary or disposable source tree. The sweep loop records an interrupted child as FAIL and may continue the loop; establish the exact cancellation behavior with a controlled fixture before choosing the correction. The observation above proves residual mutation, not every proposed root cause or arbitrary-signal behavior.

## Authority and scope

CONTRIBUTING sections 2/3 and AGENTS sections 5/8; REQUIREMENTS REQ-VER-01/02/04; the mutation driver's own exact-restoration contract; `scripts/run_all_suites.sh:run_suites`; `tb/verilator/gptp_shadow/mutants.py:apply_control`, `run_suite`, `restore`, `main`.

The gPTP processor gitlink and PP (protocol processor) gitlink remain unchanged. This is parent verification tooling, not processor RTL or a product timing change. No mutation may be removed, marked passing on a build failure, or accepted merely because cancellation returned nonzero. No general sweep parallelization or weakened suite deadline is in scope.

## Acceptance and validation

1. Establish a deterministic interrupt fixture at a known mutation-applied boundary. It must fail on the current implementation by detecting changed tracked source after shutdown. Avoid a timing-only sleep oracle; use an observable handshake.
2. A settled cleanup/isolation design keeps all tracked source bytes/modes unchanged after normal completion, named mutant failure, build failure and handled INT/TERM. A hard kill cannot execute cleanup, so its containment requirement must be met by mutation isolation or explicitly settled before Ready; do not promise impossible finally behavior.
3. A graceful stop of the outer sweep starts no later suite, terminates/reaps owned descendants and leaves attributable partial logs with no completed-PASS claim. Verify a next-suite sentinel stays unexecuted, and use process identity to distinguish exited/reaped state.
4. The original complete gPTP plane/shadow controls still run and detect their named defects. Full required parent source/candidate validation, two independent reviews with all five lenses clean, hosted checks and post-merge containment remain mandatory.

## Readiness and dependencies

Ready: [the settled isolation/cancellation decision and deterministic original-driver evidence](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/523#issuecomment-5783211002) close the design questions. Executor A182; independent internal R256 Codex and external R257 Opus are assigned. External availability remains a merge dependency. Coordinate with #517's ordinary-runner files without editing its active lane. No review finding or acceptance of #517 was waived by filing this issue; the preparation refusal was handled in the manager's disposable clone only.

Search of open and closed parent issues found no existing owner for this gPTP mutation residue. #334 concerns the separate trusted act runner; #438 concerns temporary-directory cleanup in containment tests. Neither owns this tracked-source mutation path.

[A10] Settled design and readiness for #523

The original drivers at dev483 were exercised without edits in disposable fixtures. Synthetic make waits at an explicit mutation-applied/child-started handshake; synthetic prerequisite commands replace expensive unrelated gate work. These fixtures measure orchestration only, not RTL correctness. The real mutation driver left its first named mutant in tracked KL_gptp_txret.sv after group TERM (exit -15) and group KILL (exit -9). The real sweep, signalled at the first-suite handshake along with its owned timeout child group, printed FAIL alpha then PASS omega; the next-suite sentinel executed. Original stdout/stderr, exact source blobs, file hashes/modes, diff and reproduction script are retained. No active lane, shared tool, source checkout or user checkout was mutated.

Decision: isolate every gPTP shadow mutation campaign in a fresh disposable source/build tree. Copy the required source/dependency inputs into private writable files; no hardlinks or writable links back into the caller. The original checkout stays byte/mode unchanged throughout, including hard kill. Preserve the tracked/clean-input refusal and the exact original nine mutation definitions, six unobservable reasons, named checks and build-failure distinctions. A finally block alone cannot satisfy hard-kill containment. A hard kill may leave disposable scratch or children; it must never leave mutated caller sources, and no cleanup or completed-PASS claim may be made for that path. Normal and handled INT/TERM paths must stop/reap owned descendants and clean their private workspace, with diagnostic evidence if cleanup itself fails.

The outer sweep will distinguish graceful INT/TERM cancellation from an ordinary red suite or deadline. Cancellation latches a terminal stop, starts no later suite, stops/reaps its owned command group, retains attributable partial logs and exits 130/143 without completed summary/PASS. This covers preflight and selected-suite child phases and signal arrival at transitions. Existing behavior for ordinary suite failure, masked failure, timeout UNKNOWN, shard selection, locking and deadlines remains. Never signal a foreign process or infer liveness from PID existence alone. Preserve legacy continue-after-ordinary-failure behavior.

Scope: gPTP shadow mutation orchestration, its focused lifecycle tests/Makefile/documentation, outer sweep cancellation and its focused tests/authoritative testing documentation. No generic campaign migration, suite parallelization, timeout change, product RTL/firmware, processor gitlink, retired target permission or #517 ordinary-runner edit. If new workstation-only process references encounter the bare-metal gate, only exact-file/exact-context evidence-backed masks with positive and wrong-file/line/product refusals may be proposed within this issue; no broad exemption or budget growth. Publicly report a normative conflict before dependent implementation.

Required executable validation: python3 tb/verilator/gptp_shadow/test_mutant_lifecycle.py; python3 scripts/test_suite_cancellation.py; make -C tb/verilator/gptp_shadow with scoped Verilator5.050; relevant Python/shell idiom, bare-metal positive/refusal selftests, docs and evidence/fail-fast ratchets. Both focused tests must be owned by normal supported entry points. The lifecycle controls cover normal success, named defect detection, surviving mutant, build failure, dirty/untracked input, repeat execution, handled INT/TERM and hard-kill source isolation at a deterministic handshake. Sweep controls cover signals before/during/after a child, next-suite sentinel, real owned descendant identity/reaping, partial-log attribution, timeout and ordinary-failure continuation. Restoring original unsafe behavior in a disposable control must turn the new tests red. Preserve all prior test populations and nine real mutation detections. Manager owns the full native/builder, trusted serial act, required hosted, two independent reviews, current-dev candidate and post-merge bar.

These decisions settle implementation shape without weakening acceptance1-4. Source work can start independently from dev483; final current-dev integration follows ready predecessor merges and receives fresh affected-artifact review. R245's #517 review proceeds independently. A182 is executor; cleared R256 Codex internal and R257 Opus external are reserved. External provider availability remains a merge dependency, never an implied waiver.

[Exact original-driver fixtures, raw outputs, source provenance and decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/b9a05dc9a31825fdbd7ffc5eb638dc9fe751fc6c/review-evidence/517-r1/followups/523-readiness).

[A10] READY TAKEOVER

A182 implements #523 from live dev `483a133ed08867ea0d300d2b4a027b5b48a4282f` in branch `523-isolate-mutation-cancellation`. Cleared internal R256 Codex and external R257 Opus are reserved. [Settled design, scope and exact validation](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/523#issuecomment-5783211002) apply; acceptance1-4 are preserved byte-for-byte (SHA256 `92db8ed9d36f0a7bfe9c6892eaf2b22be5b9e34fb4072af4ee766e9ee6785269`). Ready was verified before this takeover. The isolated source lane may proceed alongside #517 review without editing its runner or active checkout. Final current-dev composition and any affected review coverage follow predecessor landing. All required local/hosted gates and the external review remain mandatory.

[A182] TAKEN
Branch: 523-isolate-mutation-cancellation
Base: 483a133ed08867ea0d300d2b4a027b5b48a4282f
Authoritative references: REQ-VER-01/02/04; CONTRIBUTING sections 2/3; AGENTS sections 5/8; issue #523 acceptance 1-4; settled decision https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/523#issuecomment-5783211002.
Interpreted scope: isolate gPTP shadow mutation source/build inputs and required pinned dependencies in private writable copies; preserve all nine mutations, six unobservable reasons and existing verdict semantics. Add bounded owned-descendant cleanup for normal and handled INT/TERM paths and terminal outer-sweep cancellation across preflight, command and transition phases. Caller source remains immutable even on KILL. No product/pin, other mutation-driver, ordinary pool, deadline or population changes.
Validation plan: production-driver handshake lifecycle and sweep tests, with unsafe negative controls; complete gptp_shadow make using verified scoped Verilator 5.050 and at most eight jobs; focused normal-entry ownership, Python/shell idiom, documentation, evidence/fail-fast and bare-metal policy checks. Full parent/processor/Yosys/builder banks, trusted act, hosted checks, publication, current-dev composition and independent R256/R257 reviews remain manager-owned.
Blockers: none. Implementation source will remain clean, committed and unpublished for manager handoff.

[A182] Implementation detail within the settled #523 design

The two drivers will share a narrowly scoped workstation process owner. It will enable descendant adoption, identify owned processes by parentage and stable pid handles, latch the first INT/TERM, stop the owned command tree, escalate stubborn descendants within a bounded cleanup interval, and reap adopted children. The sweep retains its shell selection, locking, deadlines, verdicts and tally logic; a terminal shell trap prevents continuing after a cancelled foreground step. Process ownership covers selection/preflight as well as suite execution. Only exact process-inventory contexts needed by this helper and its fixtures will receive bare-metal policy controls.

Mutation inputs will be copied as new regular files from verified clean tracked bytes, including the required gPTP and axis dependencies. No reset/checkout operation will touch caller sources. Dirty/index/path refusal controls will test the input identity actually copied. The mutation and cancellation fixtures will execute production drivers and synchronize on explicit boundaries; they are orchestration evidence, while the full real gptp_shadow run remains the RTL detection evidence.

title: [Verification] Interrupted gPTP mutation campaign leaves tracked RTL modified
